title: The world of the Restoration, 1800–1848
reviewed: 2026-10-18. Each quote was copied from the linked article and is checked by npm run verify:sources.

events.title: The Second Great Awakening
events.summary: Camp meetings and revivals sweep the American frontier. Rival churches compete for converts, as Joseph Smith later recalls.

source.quote: The outpouring of religious fervor and revival began in Kentucky and Tennessee in the 1790s and early 1800s

events.title: The Stone-Campbell Restoration Movement
events.summary: Preachers seek to restore New Testament Christianity without creeds. Sidney Rigdon led such a congregation before he was baptized in 1830.

quote: The Last Will and Testament of the Springfield Presbytery (1804)
In 1832, they joined in fellowship with a handshake.

events.title: Lewis and Clark set out for the Pacific
events.summary: An army party maps the Missouri River and crosses the Rockies. Their reports open the West to American settlers.

source.quote: The Corps of Discovery departed from Camp Dubois (Camp Wood) at 4 pm on May 14, 1804.

events.title: The War of 1812
events.summary: The United States fights Britain over trade and the frontier. British troops burn Washington in 1814.

quote: The United States declared war on Britain on 18 June 1812.
ratified by the United States Senate on 17 February 1815

events.image: File:Joseph Mallord William Turner (1775-1851) - Chichester Canal - T03885 - Tate.jpg
events.title: The Year Without a Summer
events.summary: A volcanic eruption cools the world, and frost kills New England crops. The Smith family leaves Vermont for Palmyra, New York.

source.quote: The climatic aberrations of 1816 had their greatest effect on New England (US), Atlantic Canada, and Western Europe.

events.title: Shaka builds the Zulu kingdom
events.summary: A young king remakes Zulu warfare and unites many peoples by force. The Zulu become the strongest power in southern Africa.

source.quote: was the king of the Zulu Kingdom from 1816 to 1828

events.image: File:Simón Bolívar by José Gil de Castro.jpg
events.title: Bolívar proclaims Gran Colombia
events.summary: Simón Bolívar's congress joins Venezuela and New Granada in one republic. Spanish rule in South America is breaking.

source.quote: issued during the Congress of Angostura (1819)

events.image: File:Charles Bird King, Henry Clay, 1821, NGA 195003 (cropped).jpg
events.title: The Missouri Compromise
events.summary: Congress admits Missouri as a slave state and Maine as a free one. Slavery in Missouri later fuels conflict with Latter-day Saints.

source.quote: The 16th United States Congress passed the legislation on March 3, 1820

events.title: The Greek War of Independence
events.summary: Greeks rise against Ottoman rule and win a kingdom of their own. Europe's powers intervene on their side.

source.quote: fought by Greek revolutionaries against the Ottoman Empire from 1821 to 1829

events.title: Sequoyah's Cherokee syllabary
events.summary: A Cherokee silversmith invents a writing system for his language. Within a few years most Cherokees can read it.

quote: invented by Sequoyah in the late 1810s and early 1820s
By 1825, the majority of Cherokees could read and write

events.title: Brazil declares independence
events.summary: Prince Pedro breaks with Portugal and becomes Brazil's emperor.

source.quote: Officially, the date celebrated for Brazil's independence is 7 September 1822

events.title: The Monroe Doctrine
events.summary: President Monroe warns Europe against new colonies in the Americas.

source.quote: President James Monroe first articulated the doctrine on December 2, 1823

events.title: The Erie Canal opens
events.summary: A canal links the Hudson River to Lake Erie. It runs through Palmyra, where the Book of Mormon was printed.

source.quote: The entire canal was officially completed on October 26, 1825.

events.title: Andrew Jackson is president
events.summary: A frontier general becomes president and expands the power of the office. His term spans the Church's first years.

source.quote: was the seventh president of the United States from 1829 to 1837

events.image: File:President Andrew Jackson's Message to Congress "On Indian Removal", 12-06-1830, Page 1-7 (6023478288).jpg
events.title: The Indian Removal Act
events.summary: Congress authorizes moving eastern tribes west of the Mississippi. The first missionaries to the Lamanites preach to Delaware removed to Kansas.

source.quote: The Indian Removal Act of 1830 was signed into law on May 28, 1830

events.title: The first intercity railway opens
events.summary: Steam trains run between Liverpool and Manchester. Railways soon spread across Britain and the world.

source.quote: It opened on 15 September 1830 between the Lancashire towns of Liverpool and Manchester in England.

events.title: Charles Finney's Rochester revival
events.summary: A revival preacher stirs a city near Palmyra. Western New York becomes known as the burned-over district.

source.quote: In 1830-1831, he led a revival in Rochester, New York

events.title: Nat Turner's rebellion
events.summary: Enslaved people in Virginia rise in revolt and are crushed. Southern states pass harsher slave laws.

source.quote: a slave rebellion that took place in Southampton County, Virginia, United States, in August 1831

events.title: South Carolina nullifies the tariff
events.summary: South Carolina declares a federal tariff void, and Jackson threatens force. D&C 87, given that December, foresees war beginning there.

source.quote: on November 24, 1832, a state convention adopted the Ordinance of Nullification

events.title: The Black Hawk War
events.summary: Sauk leader Black Hawk returns to Illinois and is driven out by militia. The fighting opens the region to settlers.

source.quote: On April 5, 1832, the British Band entered Illinois once again.

events.title: Cholera reaches North America
events.summary: A worldwide cholera pandemic reaches Canada and the United States. It strikes Zion's Camp in Missouri in 1834.

quote: In 1832, the epidemic reached Quebec, Ontario, and Nova Scotia in Canada and Detroit and New York City in the United States.
It reached the Pacific coast of North America between 1832 and 1834.

events.image: File:The Anti-Slavery Society Convention, 1840 by Benjamin Robert Haydon.jpg
events.title: Britain abolishes slavery in its colonies
events.summary: Parliament passes a law to free the enslaved across most of the British Empire.

source.quote: While the 1833 Act was a landmark, it did not end slavery throughout the entire British sphere of influence.

events.title: Texas wins independence from Mexico
events.summary: Settlers in Texas revolt and found a republic. The Alamo falls before the victory at San Jacinto.

source.quote: The Texas Revolution (October 2, 1835-April 21, 1836)

events.title: The Great Trek in southern Africa
events.summary: Dutch-speaking settlers leave the Cape by wagon for the interior. Their trek parallels other mass migrations of the age.

source.quote: from the Cape Colony into the interior of modern South Africa from 1836 onwards

events.image: File:Albert Bierstadt - Emigrants Crossing the Plains (1867).jpg
events.title: Wagon trains start west on the Oregon Trail
events.summary: Migrants begin crossing the plains by wagon. The pioneers later follow the same river valleys to the Salt Lake Valley.

source.quote: By 1836, when the first migrant wagon train was organized in Independence, Missouri

events.title: The Panic of 1837
events.summary: Banks fail across the United States, and a long depression follows. The Kirtland Safety Society collapses in the same crisis.

source.quote: The bank run came to a head on May 10, 1837, when banks in New York City ran out of gold and silver.

events.title: Victoria becomes queen
events.summary: An 18-year-old queen begins a reign of 63 years. The first Latter-day Saint missionaries reach England the same summer.

source.quote: Queen of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland from 20 June 1837 until her death in 1901

events.title: The Cherokee are forced west
events.summary: Soldiers march the Cherokee to Indian Territory, and thousands die. The same year Latter-day Saints are driven from Missouri.

source.quote: The Cherokee removal in 1838 was the last forced removal east of the Mississippi

events.title: Photography is introduced
events.summary: Louis Daguerre's process makes the first practical photographs. Portraits of Church leaders soon follow.

source.quote: Invented by Louis Daguerre and introduced worldwide in 1839

events.title: Morse sends "What hath God wrought"
events.summary: The first long telegraph line opens between Washington and Baltimore. News now moves faster than any rider.

source.quote: On May 24, 1844, the line was officially opened as Morse sent the now-famous words

events.title: The Millerites' Great Disappointment
events.summary: Followers of William Miller expect Christ's return on a set day. When it passes, the movement splinters.

source.quote: When Jesus did not appear by October 22, 1844, Miller and his followers were disappointed

events.title: The Great Famine in Ireland
events.summary: Potato blight brings mass starvation to Ireland. More than two million people emigrate.

source.quote: a period of mass starvation and disease in Ireland from 1845 to 1852

events.title: The Mexican–American War
events.summary: The United States invades Mexico and takes the Southwest. The Mormon Battalion marches to California in this war.

source.quote: (April 25, 1846-February 2, 1848) was an invasion of Mexico by the United States

events.title: Gold is found in California
events.summary: Workers at Sutter's Mill find gold, and a rush begins. Former Mormon Battalion men are among the workers.

source.quote: which began on January 24, 1848

events.title: The revolutions of 1848
events.summary: Uprisings spread across Europe, demanding constitutions and national rights. Most are put down within two years.

source.quote: between January 1848 and October 1849

events.title: The Seneca Falls Convention
events.summary: The first women's rights convention meets in western New York. Its declaration calls for women's right to vote.

source.quote: it spanned two days over July 19-20, 1848
